initial_pit_state_design.semantics: at T driver is in admitted pit lifecycle state; simulator initialises driver with last causally valid race-distance state + pit lifecycle state + sampled additional pit delay; during delay driver makes no normal racing progress; after delay resumes accepted MC2-E dynamics; others continue; no teleportation, no fabricated gap reset, no historical actual return time
initial_pit_state_design.component: raceintel/simulation/pit_lifecycle.py (isolated, repo conventions; identify/use precomputed admitted pit state, sample additional delay, provide MC2 initial pit condition; no network/results/future)

kernel_boundary.finding: MC2 represents post-T pits ONLY as forward R6 decisions (stint target age -> pit_effective_loss_s added once, pit_count++, tyre reset). No driver can begin inside a pit process: all drivers start ACTIVE with race_time_s and are immediately scheduled for the next lap. An initial remaining pit delay would belong architecturally to SimulationState/adapter output (initial condition) + a hold in the event loop (kernel). Finish order is sorted (finish_time, driver_id) over full-distance finishers; no terminal classification exists (DNF unsupported).
kernel_boundary.detail: initial-condition extension (presence/adapter) plus a local event-loop hold/resume; R3/R6 pace science untouched. Verdict is conditional: reached only if science + materiality pass; with REJECT verdicts above, boundary is NOT crossed (no implementation).
